audit: P0-1 construct-validity / matcher false-negative audit (Reviewer M1)
method: Stratified random sample of executed-but-unmatched benchmark cases (executed==True AND match==False), restricted to strong configs (condA/condC families) where the executed-unmatched pool is most informative; each case independently judged for engineering-equivalence with an adversarial refutation pass on every claimed false-negative.

false_negative_rate.definition: upheld false_negatives / total judged (ambiguous counted in denominator, excluded from numerator)

breakdowns.fn_subtype_note: 100% of upheld false-negatives are 'parser_extraction' (correct value present in exec_output but the numeric/bool parser failed to extract it from multi-line/labeled output). Zero false-negatives were due to tolerance band or unit/format equivalence after the adversarial pass (2 tolerance-flagged near-misses and the 1 explicitly downgraded item were all refuted to genuine_error).

uniformity.interpretation: False-negatives are not concentrated in any tier or model (every tier's Wilson CI overlaps the pooled rate; FNs appear across 6 of 15 models and 4 of 5 tiers). The matcher is therefore a CONSERVATIVE BUT UNBIASED estimator: it underscores absolute accuracy by a small uniform amount that does not differentially advantage or penalise any model, so cross-model rankings/comparisons are not distorted.

pool_mapping.cross_validation_note: The matcher's own match_failure_reasons log 31,574 cannot_parse cases (25.4% of the unmatched pool); the audit's 8% upheld-FN rate is well below that ceiling, confirming that most parse-failures are still genuine errors and only a minority are recoverable engineering-correct answers.

accuracy_shift_bound.interpretation: If EVERY estimated false-negative in the entire pool were corrected, overall benchmark accuracy would rise by ~1.3 pp (point; <=2.5 pp at the 95% upper bound). Reported accuracies are therefore a slight, uniform lower bound; the gap is far smaller than the cross-model and cross-condition effects the paper reports.

recommendation.verdict: CONVERTS M1 from attack to defense
recommendation.rationale: The false-negative rate is low (8%, 95% CI 4.1-15.0%) and uniform across tiers and models (all tier CIs overlap the pooled rate; FNs spread across 6/15 models, 4/5 tiers). Because the bias is small and model-agnostic, the matcher is a conservative-but-unbiased estimator and cross-model comparisons are not distorted. No accuracy CLAIM needs to be retracted; the only honest caveat is a one-line statement that reported accuracies are a slight lower bound (overall <=+2.5 pp if all FNs were recovered).
recommendation.required_softening: Minor only: add a single sentence that reported accuracies are a conservative lower bound due to occasional parser-extraction misses, with the audited <=2.5pp ceiling. All single 100% upheld-FN subtype = parser_extraction also motivates an optional matcher improvement (robust extraction from labeled multi-line output) as future work, but is not required for the current claims.
